an3.2:1.1: “Bhikkhus, the fool is characterized by his actions; the wise person is characterized by his actions. Wisdom shines in its manifestation.
an3.2:1.2: “Bhikkhus, one who possesses three qualities should be known as a fool.
an3.2:1.4: Bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, and mental misconduct.
an3.2:1.5: One who possesses these three qualities should be known as a fool.
an3.2:2.1: One who possesses three qualities should be known as a wise person.
an3.2:2.3: Bodily good conduct, verbal good conduct, and mental good conduct.
an3.2:2.4: One who possesses these three qualities should be known as a wise person.
an3.2:3.1: “Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus:
an3.2:3.2: ‘We will avoid the three qualities possessing which one is known as a fool, and we will undertake and observe the three qualities possessing which one is known as a wise person.’
an3.2:3.3: It is in this way that you should train yourselves.”
